test_only_reason: No implementation changes: order_children and Evaluate already produce the Sec 4.2 child order. The defect is in test data: the checker self-test traces (and the README) assumed child orders [P, c] / [a, b] and gaps g(P,c)=5, g(c,P)=8, so the align trace posted the supplemental offer at b = 8 instead of a = 11. The checker cannot detect child order (it checks I1-I8 and the protocol), so the wrong trace passed. The corrected traces and new checks that tie them to order_children and to Evaluate pass on the existing implementation; there is no new behaviour to drive with a RED.

test_reduction_allowed.reason: Correct the hand traces chain/align of test_eval_invariants.cpp (expected values change). Sec 4.2 l.726-730 and Lemma 4.4 (l.735, reverse finishing order): with no light arcs, the DFS roots at R are P (provisional rep a, F preorder 0) then c, so the rank order is [c, P], rep(P) = a, g(c, P) = D_F(a, c) (5 in chain, 11 in align); at P it is [b, a], g(b, a) = D_F(a, b). The old traces assumed [P, c] / [a, b] and g(P,c)=5, g(c,P)=8 (asymmetric, against g(i,j)=g(j,i) in Lemma 4.4): in align, Sec 4.3 l.826 then puts the R-slot supplemental offer at rep(P) = a with max{6, 0 + 0 + 11} = 11, not at b = 8. The leaf-layout intervals in on_open/on_scan_* follow the rank order (c, b, a), not (a, b, c). Evidence: the new checks (supplemental offers recomputed from order_children, event-by-event comparison with evaluate) fail on the old traces (align: state 1 vs 0, value 8 vs 11; chain: states {0,1,2} vs {2,1,0} at the root open) and the order_children output matches the hand derivation.
